# Jowangshin walks into a agriculture, food & harvest firm

Walk into any agriculture, food & harvest outfit and watch for ten minutes. You will see a very old act performed with newer props. The act has a name. It is **Jowangshin**.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Munjeon Bonpuri: Yeosan Buin's Death and Return.** The fullest origin myth of the hearth goddess is the Jeju epic Munjeon Bonpuri, chanted by the island's shamanic simbang.  Its heroine — Yeosan Buin in most versions, Noga-danpung-agissi in others — marries Mun-doryeong and suffers at the hands of her mother-in-law, who slanders her until the household casts her out; she dies unjustly and her small sons are left to wander.  The boys win help from Sumyeong-janggun, the god of longevity, whose mugwort water raises the dead: she rises, and in the epic's decisive scene the heavenly king Cheonjiwang assigns the couple their posts — she becomes Jowang, the kitchen goddess who keeps watch over every hearth, and her husband becomes Seongju, the guardian of the house-site itself.

**The Five Taboos of the Hearth.** Around Jowangshin grew a code of kitchen conduct, the so-called five taboos, recorded in folklore collections and still repeated by older Koreans: do not curse or quarrel in the kitchen; do not sit on the hearth; do not rest your feet on the hearth or against the cooking pots; keep the kitchen clean; and never act disrespectfully before the fire.  Each rule worked twice.  Practically it kept the cooking space sanitary and the fire safe; spiritually it kept the household's daily conduct out of the report the kitchen god was compiling.

## Not the First Rebrand

Jowangshin is closely parallel to the Chinese Zao Jun (Kitchen God), and the two figures influenced each other across a thousand years of Sino-Korean exchange — the Korean name itself is a translation of the Chinese title, and the Songje date sits near the Chinese 'Little New Year' sending-off of the Stove God on the twenty-third of the twelfth month.  Yet the Korean figure has her own origin epic, the Munjeon Bonpuri, and is embedded in a distinct shamanic ritual world. The office is only the latest translation.
